purpose: Fixed report fields for independent simulated beginner participant 1; observations are restricted to visible UI and mouse actions.
persona: Simulated beginner, first introduction to RILL, interested in a short relaxed lo-fi sketch.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: The empty-lane hint, Assign instrument, Pencil length dragging, onscreen naming keyboard, and prefilled file dialogs let me complete the task with mouse input. Exact trimming took several corrective gestures.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark layout, teal waveforms, readable notes, and clearly grouped transport looked appealing and coherent. Audio and MIDI used similar colors, so their differentiation was mostly their contents.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Drawing, duplication, and navigation responded promptly. Duplication built both tracks together quickly. Native dialogs needed a later capture to finish rendering, and WAV export showed elapsed progress before completion; this is a subjective session rating, not a benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Only small uncertainties: Loop clip did not visibly create repetitions, Duplicate first selected a tool and then required a clip click, and selected clips needed separate endpoint trims. Hints and exact drag tooltips resolved these.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: Audio arrangement, MIDI drawing, native VST assignment, project naming/saving, and both exports were available and visibly worked for this sketch. Broader production features and audible results were not tested.

findings.observation: Double-clicking the empty lane using its visible MIDI hint opened Device library; Assign instrument created a pattern and a track labeled with Rill Lab Sine.
Pencil drags drew labeled notes with visible lengths, and drawing beyond the initial clip end expanded the MIDI pattern.
The Loop clip menu action did not visibly produce repeated clips. The Duplicate toolbar button activated a tool first; its Click a clip to duplicate hint explained the required next click.
A rectangle selection and Duplicate click copied both selected tracks together; repeated clicks on the new groups extended the arrangement to 34.286 seconds.
Trimming the selected audio and MIDI endings required separate edge drags. The first attempt at the 30-second grid line left a visible project duration of 30.268 seconds.
Holding a trim drag displayed exact End and Duration values. Small corrections brought both track endings to 30.000 seconds, also shown in the project header.
Play changed to Pause, and a subsequent screenshot showed the playhead advanced with both audio and instrument meters lit. Stop returned the transport to the beginning.
Rename project offered an onscreen Keyboard with Clear and Space. Mouse clicks entered soft rain; Save as and export dialogs automatically used that chosen name.
The first Save as dialog capture was black and the first MIDI dialog capture had an empty location/list; a subsequent capture showed each rendered correctly without recovery actions.

WAV export displayed its 30-second arrangement scope, sample format, and effect-tail option. After tails were unchecked, export showed elapsed status and later a success checkmark. MIDI export also showed a success checkmark.

outcome.status: Completed through the visible UI: named and saved project, exact 30.000-second arrangement displayed, WAV and MIDI export success notices seen. File contents remain independently unverified.
outcome.composition: Two tracks at 112 BPM: unmodified startup Circuit rhythm audio duplicated into four adjacent clips, with the last shortened to two bars; a manually drawn twelve-note motif with paired lower notes and upper notes across four bars, duplicated alongside the audio with its final clip shortened to two bars. Intended as a short relaxed sketch; audible musical character was not assessed.
outcome.playback_observed: Play became Pause; the yellow playhead advanced and transport displayed 004.02.85 in a later screenshot. Both track meters were illuminated. Stop returned the transport to 001.01.00. No heard audio claim.

limitations: No source, project state API, or output file-content inspection; saved/exported paths are derived from visible native dialogs and completion indicators. Independent coordinator verification follows.
Audio was not auditioned; playhead and meters establish visible playback only, not audible quality or the success of a particular lo-fi sound.
The timer-paced virtual audio sink and installed laboratory sine VST do not establish physical audio latency, hardware behavior, or compatibility with other plug-ins.
Elapsed session time includes screenshots, tools, and reporting overhead and is not a performance benchmark.
